addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# Todo

This file contains near term tasks with a short description
and reference links to more details.

Intro paragraphs in `## Todo` and `## Bugs` should begin every
line with 1 leading space so they don't match the `^\d+\. `
pattern that locates numbered entries; 2 or 3 spaces also work.

## In Progress

When a `## Todo` item is picked up, its text **moves** here
(never copied — one home per text). The picked-up task is a
`###` heading; a multi-cycle program adds one level — the
program is the `###` and its current stage a `####` (headings
give the current work durable anchors, which numbered Todo
entries can't). The problem overview is followed by the
"plan" — a bulleted list of the development "ladder". Each
rung is prepended with its commit reference — a literal
`[[N]]` placeholder until the commit is pushed, then
backfilled to a real file-local `[[n]]` ref (same pattern as
the chores As-built rungs):
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-0 blah (done)
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-1 blah blah (current)
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-2 blah blah blah
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y close-out and validation

### Refactor: typed jj facade → jj-lib in-process; end subprocess spawning

Version-control operations were ~30 hand-rolled `run("jj", …)`
spawns plus every mutation, with per-module private wrappers
and raw-git vestiges in init — stderr parsing instead of typed
errors, and jj's single-attempt index-lock acquisition (the
push `bookmark-set` lock race in [bugs.md](notes/bugs.md))
can't be retried where it fails. A multi-ladder program; the
staged plan, design detail, and the eight absorbed former
Todos live in
[refactor-20260716.md](notes/refactor-20260716.md).

Program ladder — one rung per cycle (adjacent stages
consolidated 2026-07-24; rung titles are the anticipated
close-out commit titles; unshipped versions are provisional —
jj-lib may split into two cycles). Shipped-rung refs point at
close-out commits on `refactor-vc-x1`, treated as permanent:
the branch is long-lived and lands on main merge-only, never
rebased.

111	## Preparation
112	
113	The cycle's first commit (`X.Y.Z-0`), when the cycle needs
114	setup (a lightweight cycle omits it — see
115	[versioning.md](versioning.md#step-numbering)):
116	
117	- **Bump the version-of-record** to `X.Y.Z-0`. Where it
118	  lives, the suffix scheme, and any derived files (a
119	  lockfile, a sourced manifest version) are
120	  project-specific — see [versioning.md](versioning.md).
121	- **Move a `## Todo` item** (if the cycle has one) into
122	  `## In Progress` and the todo item should have:
123	  - A **bold title line** — that will be the chores
124	    section header, minus the `## ` prefix.
125	  - A **succinct problem statement**; add if one is needed
126	  - A **plan ladder**.
127	- **Open the [chores section](#chores-sections)** —
128	  append a `##` header with the title it records — the
129	  cycle's anticipated close-out title.
130	
131	## Work-N
132	
133	The cycle's work commits (`X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, …)
134	implement the change. As many as needed:
135	
136	- Each commit runs through the
137	  **[per-commit flow](#per-commit-flow)**.
138	- **Interim pushes** are optional (backup, progress
139	  visibility).
140	- Close-out is the only mandatory push (see
141	  [Pushing](#pushing)).
142	- **Subdivide into a sub-cycle** if a Work commit's
143	  scope grows enough (see
144	  [Sub-cycle ladders](#sub-cycle-ladders)).
145	
146	## Close-out
147	
148	The cycle's last commit (bare `X.Y.Z`) does bookkeeping
149	only — the commit body describes that bookkeeping, not
150	what happens post-squash:
151	
152	- **Move the picked-up item** from `## In Progress` to a
153	  one-line entry (with a chores `[N]` ref) in `## Done`.
154	- **Finalize the chores section** (opened during Preparation
155	  and grown per commit — see [Chores sections](#chores-sections)):
156	  - The problem statement is already the chores intro (written
157	    when the section was opened) and the plan ladder is already
158	    the `### As-built ladder` (a rung appended per commit), so
159	    close-out only *finalizes*, it does not cut-and-paste.
160	  - Sync the chores header to the **final** commit title if the
161	    cycle's scope shifted; update every anchor back-reference.
162	  - Add any `### design subsections`; optional `### Outcome`
163	    notes.
164	  - Replace the `## In Progress` cycle block with
165	    `_No cycle currently in progress._`.
166	- **Update `notes/README.md`** if functionality changed
167	  (new flags, new subcommands, changed behavior).
168	
169	Whether to **squash** the cycle into one commit before the
170	publishing push, or push as-is, is decided at push time —
171	see [Pushing](#pushing).
172	
173	## Numbering
174	
175	Each commit's phase is encoded in the version suffix — `-0`
176	Preparation, `-1`/`-2`/… Work, bare `X.Y.Z` Close-out,
177	recursively for sub-cycles. The full scheme — disambiguation,
178	nesting, optional Preparation, the project's version-of-record
179	format, and the per-phase bump — lives in
180	[versioning.md](versioning.md#step-numbering), which is the
181	single source of truth for this repo's versioning.
182	
183	## Per-commit flow
184	
185	Every commit (Preparation, each Work commit, Close-out) goes
186	through:
187	
188	1. **Mark this commit `(current)`** as the first edit in
189	   `TODO.md > ## In Progress` (`TODO.md` is at the repo
190	   root).
191	2. **Do the work** (see [Iterative work](#iterative-work)
192	   for the loop-and-squash technique).
193	3. **Flip this commit `(current)` → `(done)`** in `## In
194	   Progress` — before the cargo cycle and the commit.
195	4. **Validate the artifact** — a medium-specific step, skip-able
196	   for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out. For the Rust
197	   example the cargo cycle is:
198	   1. `cargo fmt`
199	   2. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
200	   3. `cargo test`
201	   4. `cargo install --path . --locked`
202	   5. (re-test if anything substantive changed)
203	5. **Work review.** Stop *before* writing any description;
204	   tell the user "ready to commit." The user reviews the
205	   changes and we iterate until complete.
206	6. **Write the commit description** — see
207	   [Commit description](#commit-description).
208	7. **Commit Description review.** Show the title + body
209	   and stop. The user reviews the description. Iterate.
210	8. **Commit.** `jj commit -m "title" -m "body" -R .` for
211	   the work repo, `-R .claude` for the bot repo (`-R` last
212	   keeps the verb visible):
213	
214	   ```
215	   jj commit -m \
216	   "<type>: <short description>" \
217	   -m "<intro paragraph>
218	
219	   - file1: gist
220	   - file2: gist
221	
222	   ochid: /.claude/<chid>" \
223	   -R .
224	   ```
225	
226	**Two overrides apply:**
227	
228	- **Deviation or question** — any time the work deviates
229	  from the agreed plan, or a question arises, stop and
230	  surface it; don't push through.
231	- **ESC-ESC** — the user can interrupt at any point to pull
232	  a review or question forward.

  - A **plan ladder**.
- **Open the [chores section](#chores-sections)** —

  cycle's anticipated close-out title.

## Work-N

The cycle's work commits (`X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, …)
implement the change. As many as needed:

- Each commit runs through the
  **[per-commit flow](#per-commit-flow)**.
- **Interim pushes** are optional (backup, progress

- Close-out is the only mandatory push (see
  [Pushing](#pushing)).
- **Subdivide into a sub-cycle** if a Work commit's
  scope grows enough (see
  [Sub-cycle ladders](#sub-cycle-ladders)).

## Close-out

The cycle's last commit (bare `X.Y.Z`) does bookkeeping
only — the commit body describes that bookkeeping, not
what happens post-squash:

- **Move the picked-up item** from `## In Progress` to a
  one-line entry (with a chores `[N]` ref) in `## Done`.
- **Finalize the chores section** (opened during Preparation
  and grown per commit — see [Chores sections](#chores-sections)):
  - The problem statement is already the chores intro (written
    when the section was opened) and the plan ladder is already
    the `### As-built ladder` (a rung appended per commit), so
    close-out only *finalizes*, it does not cut-and-paste.
  - Sync the chores header to the **final** commit title if the
    cycle's scope shifted; update every anchor back-reference.
  - Add any `### design subsections`; optional `### Outcome`
    notes.
  - Replace the `## In Progress` cycle block with
    `_No cycle currently in progress._`.
- **Update `notes/README.md`** if functionality changed
  (new flags, new subcommands, changed behavior).

Whether to **squash** the cycle into one commit before the
publishing push, or push as-is, is decided at push time —
see [Pushing](#pushing).

## Numbering

Each commit's phase is encoded in the version suffix — `-0`
Preparation, `-1`/`-2`/… Work, bare `X.Y.Z` Close-out,
recursively for sub-cycles. The full scheme — disambiguation,
nesting, optional Preparation, the project's version-of-record
format, and the per-phase bump — lives in
[versioning.md](versioning.md#step-numbering), which is the
single source of truth for this repo's versioning.

## Per-commit flow

Every commit (Preparation, each Work commit, Close-out) goes
through:

1. **Mark this commit `(current)`** as the first edit in
   `TODO.md > ## In Progress` (`TODO.md` is at the repo
   root).
2. **Do the work** (see [Iterative work](#iterative-work)
   for the loop-and-squash technique).
3. **Flip this commit `(current)` → `(done)`** in `## In
   Progress` — before the cargo cycle and the commit.
4. **Validate the artifact** — a medium-specific step, skip-able
   for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out. For the Rust
   example the cargo cycle is:
   1. `cargo fmt`
   2. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
   3. `cargo test`
   4. `cargo install --path . --locked`
   5. (re-test if anything substantive changed)
5. **Work review.** Stop *before* writing any description;
   tell the user "ready to commit." The user reviews the
   changes and we iterate until complete.
6. **Write the commit description** — see
   [Commit description](#commit-description).
7. **Commit Description review.** Show the title + body

8. **Commit.** `jj commit -m "title" -m "body" -R .` for
   the work repo, `-R .claude` for the bot repo (`-R` last
   keeps the verb visible):

   ```
   jj commit -m \
   "<type>: <short description>" \
   -m "<intro paragraph>

   - file1: gist
   - file2: gist

   -R .
   ```

**Two overrides apply:**

- **Deviation or question** — any time the work deviates
  from the agreed plan, or a question arises, stop and
  surface it; don't push through.
- **ESC-ESC** — the user can interrupt at any point to pull

message.content: So when I clone an old repo it still works, should be suggest/warn that the vc-config has changed and it should be updated?

content.text:
Short answer: an old repo doesn't silently "still work" — the design is a loud, actionable rejection rather than a warning — but your question did surface one real gap in `clone`.

The current behavior, by path:

- **Any resolver-touching command** (`chid`, `sync`, `push`, `config --validate`, …) in a legacy workspace: `find_workspace_root_from` still *finds* the legacy root (both generations — pre-0.75 `path`/`other-repo` and now the 0.75.x root-anchored `work`/`bot`), and `reject_legacy_config` fails fast with the fix-it message showing the exact per-side `[repos]` rewrite. So the "suggest it should be updated" part already exists — it's just delivered as an error, not a warning. That's deliberate: the readers treat unknown keys as absent, so proceeding with a warning would silently degrade a dual workspace to single-repo — worse than stopping. And published history is unaffected: `/` and `/.claude` ochid trailers stay resolvable as historical labels (rung -3 formalizes that).

- **`vc-x1 clone` of an old repo — the gap.** `clone.rs:215-218` resolves the bot dir with `match configured_bot_dir(target_dir) { Ok(Some(p)) => p, _ => target_dir.join(".claude") }`. The `_` arm swallows the legacy-rejection *error* the same as a missing config, so cloning a legacy repo quietly proceeds with the default `.claude` fallback — and the user only hits the fix-it message on the *next* command. Clone is exactly where "you've just fetched an old repo, its config needs updating" should be surfaced, and today it's the one entry point that hides it.

So I'd frame the choice as:

1. **Surface the legacy error at clone time** (recommended) — split the `_` arm: absent config → fallback as today; legacy/config error → fail (or complete the clone and print the rewrite guidance). Small, fits this cycle's spirit.
2. **A migration helper** (`config --migrate` writing the `[repos]` rewrite) — convenient, but it's "automatic fixing", which this project has deliberately declined before; the hand edit is two small files.
3. **Warn-and-continue legacy reading** — I'd avoid it: it means carrying both schemas in every reader indefinitely for an unreleased schema with one known external workspace.

The plain version: old repos already get told, loudly and with exact instructions, that their config needs updating — except when you clone one, where the message is currently swallowed until the next command. That clone gap is the thing worth fixing.

Want me to fold the clone-time surfacing into this rung (it's schema-adjacent), slot it as a later rung in this cycle, or park it as a Todo?

content.text:
The backward-compat rider is in — **ready to commit** (0.76.0-1, now including the clone bug fix). What the rider adds:

- **`common::legacy_configured_bot_dir`** — a deliberate backward-compat read of both rejected generations' bot declaration (0.75.x `workspace.bot`, pre-0.75 `workspace.other-repo`). Only bootstrap surfaces use it; every resolver still hard-rejects with the fix-it.
- **`clone_dual`** — the `_` catch-all that swallowed the legacy error is split into explicit arms: new schema → declared dir; no config → `.claude` default; legacy → clone completes with the *legacy-declared* bot dir plus a `warn` telling the user to update to `[repos]`; unreadable → warn + default.
- **`symlink::default_bot_target`** — follows the same legacy read, so the Claude Code symlink points at the actual bot dir (the smoke test caught it targeting `.claude` while the bot repo landed in `.bot`).
- **Fix-it message** — the rewrite example now echoes the workspace's actual bot dir name instead of hardcoded `.claude`.

Verified end-to-end with a scratch legacy workspace using a non-default `.bot` dir: clone completes both sides into the right places with the warning; a scoped command afterward prints the rewrite with `bot = ".bot"`; the only smoke-rig failure was the sandbox's read-only `~/.claude/projects` on the final symlink write (environmental). Scratch tree removed; fmt/clippy clean, all 517 tests pass, binary reinstalled.

One new `unwrap_or_else` alert per convention: the fix-it message's bot-name fallback (`// OK: default dir name for the rewrite example` — worst case the example shows `.claude`).

Please review — after your OK I'll draft the commit description.

vc-x1-dev 0.76.0-0

Commit both repos, push the work repo's BOOKMARK, and
squash-push the bot repo's `main` — one resumable command.

Collapses the manual commit-push-publish ceremony into a
single subcommand with two interactive approval gates and a
state machine with persistent progress so interruptions can
resume without re-doing completed stages.

Stages: preflight (tracking / bot-published / sync checks —
no build steps; run project checks yourself before pushing)
→ review (approve diff)
→ message ($EDITOR / --title+--body, approve text) →
commit-work → commit-bot (skipped if clean) → bookmark-set
(work repo → <bookmark>, bot repo → main) → push-work →
squash-push-bot. Failures in commit-work / commit-bot /
bookmark-set roll both repos back via
`jj op restore` to the snapshot recorded before commit-work.
After push-work succeeds the remote boundary is crossed and
recovery is forward-only.

Non-interactive use: pass both --title and --body plus --yes
to skip the review gate. Saved state carries title/body
across resumes so only the first invocation needs them.

Usage: vc-x1-dev push [OPTIONS] [BOOKMARK]

Arguments:
  [BOOKMARK]
          Bookmark to advance in the work repo (positional form of
          `--bookmark`). The bot repo always advances `main`.
          
          Accepting a positional lets the common case read as `vc-x1 push main`
          without the `--bookmark` ceremony; `--bookmark` is kept as an alias
          for scripts and for composition with other args. The two forms
          conflict if both supplied.

Options:
      --bookmark <BOOKMARK>
          Bookmark to advance in the work repo (flag form; see positional)

  -V, --version
          Print the `vc-x1 X.Y.Z` banner as the first line, then continue. With
          no subcommand, prints the banner and exits.
          
          Replaces clap's auto-version (which would exit after printing): the
          banner now rides along with normal subcommand execution rather than
          gating it, so scripts can capture the version *and* the command's
          output in one invocation.

      --restart
          Clear any saved state file and start from stage 1

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --from <STAGE>
          Explicit stage to jump to (advanced / debug use)

          Possible values:
          - preflight:       Verify bookmark tracking, the bot-published
            invariant, and sync state
          - review:          Present diff for the first approval gate
          - message:         Compose / edit the commit message; present for
            second gate
          - commit-work:     Commit the work repo
          - commit-bot:      Commit the `.claude` bot repo (skipped if empty)
          - bookmark-set:    Advance each repo's bookmark to its `@-`: work →
            `<bookmark>`, bot → `main`
          - push-work:       `jj git push --bookmark <b> -R .`
          - squash-push-bot: In-process squash of `.claude`'s trailing session
            writes + push `main`

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

      --step
          Pause between every stage for an interactive approval gate

      --status
          Print where the saved state thinks we are and exit

      --recheck
          Re-run `preflight` even on resume (default: skip if last run
          succeeded)

      --no-squash-push
          Stop before `squash-push-bot` so it can be run manually

      --dry-run
          Print the exact commands for every stage without side effects

      --title <STR>
          Commit title (skip `$EDITOR` for the message stage)

      --body <STR>
          Commit body (skip `$EDITOR` for the message stage)

  -y, --yes
          Auto-approve interactive prompts (review gate, message-edit
          confirmation). Required when `--title` / `--body` aren't both supplied
          in non-interactive contexts

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

329	## Pushing
330	
331	### Policy
332	
333	Push is **discretionary** during the cycle (backup,
334	progress visibility) and **mandatory at close-out** —
335	the cycle's result must be published.
336	
337	**Approval is per-push.** Every push — any repo, any kind:
338	cycle push, interim backup, recovery/surgery force-push —
339	happens only after the user has reviewed the changes to be
340	published and explicitly approved that specific push.
341	Approval of a plan that *includes* a push does not authorize
342	the push itself; stop and ask again at the moment of pushing.
343	
344	**Default is interactive; an explicit scoped delegation waives
345	the gates.** The gates above — per-push approval, the
346	commit-description review (show title+body and stop), and the
347	hard stop after push/squash-push — are the *interactive
348	default*.
349	They yield when the user **explicitly** delegates a complete,
350	bounded task and authorizes carrying it through ("do all of X
351	and push each step, don't check in"). The bot then proceeds
352	through that task's commits and pushes without stopping, and
353	continues past each push to the next step. Conditions:
354	
355	- **Explicit grant** — never inferred from a task merely being
356	  well-scoped; the user's words must authorize unattended
357	  completion. "Commit and push" (or "then push") names the
358	  destination, not a waiver: it authorizes the push *after*
359	  the normal work review and description review, not skipping
360	  them. Only wording that explicitly waives the stops ("don't
361	  check in", "no need to review", "carry it through
362	  unattended") waives them.
363	- **Bounded goal** — covers the named task only; does not carry
364	  to the next task or a vaguer follow-on.
365	- **Destructive ops still pause** — delegation covers the task's
366	  ordinary commits and pushes; it does *not* pre-authorize a
367	  genuinely irreversible action (force-push over published
368	  history, history rewrite, deleting a remote branch). Those can
369	  permanently destroy work and aren't a normal cycle step, so the
370	  bot flags one before acting. An ordinary delegated cycle never
371	  reaches this.
372	- **Still transparent** — report each commit/push as it lands
373	  (title + outcome) so the user can catch up.
374	- **When in doubt, ask** — ambiguous authorization falls back to
375	  per-push approval.
376	
377	### Shape at close-out push
378	
379	At close-out the cycle's *work* is done; its *published
380	shape* is the remaining choice, made at push time. Surface
381	the options and get user approval before pushing — once on
382	the target, changing shape is a remote rewrite (force-push,
383	needs approval), so choose deliberately.
384	
385	- **Squash to one commit** — single entry on the target.
386	  Right for straightforward changes where the Work-N is
387	  focused on one or two files.
388	- **Merge non-ff** *(current default)* — `main` gains a
389	  merge commit (`X.Y.Z`); cycle commits stay reachable via
390	  two parents. `jj log -r ..@ -n <N>` shows the trapezoidal
391	  shape. See [Merge non-ff recipe](#merge-non-ff-recipe)
392	  for the full setup sequence.
393	- **Keep separate** — one commit per cycle entry on
394	  `main`. Use when the decomposition itself is
395	  informative. Each chores section keeps its own header /
396	  `Commits:` ref; no consolidation churn.
397	
398	Set up squash/merge before invoking `vc-x1 push`; use
399	`jj git push` directly for non-standard shapes.
400	
401	### Merge non-ff recipe
402	
403	Setting up a [Merge non-ff](#shape-at-close-out-push)
404	close-out is a fixed sequence. `<closeout>` is the cycle's
405	close-out commit, `<prev>` the previous cycle's close-out
406	(the current `main` tip), `<work-tip>` the cycle's last
407	Work commit:
408	
409	1. **Rebase the close-out into a merge** — `jj rebase -r
410	   <closeout> --onto <prev> --onto <work-tip>`.
411	   - `-r <closeout>` keeps the `<closeout>` commit in place.
412	   - `--onto <prev>` becomes its first parent (trunk).
413	   - `--onto <work-tip>` becomes the second parent.
414	
415	   Together these make `<closeout>` a merge of
416	   `<prev>` + `<work-tip>`, forming a trapezoidal commit.
417	2. **Use `jj new <merge>`** to add an empty `@` above the
418	   merge. The rebase left `@` *on* the now-content-bearing
419	   merge, which git/IDE diff views show as uncommitted;
420	   `jj new` restores the clean empty `@` on top.
421	3. **Push** — `jj git push --bookmark main -R .`.
422	
423	**Post-hoc caveat.** If the cycle was already pushed
424	[Keep separate](#shape-at-close-out-push) its commits are
425	immutable: the rebase needs `--ignore-immutable` and the
426	push force-updates `main`.
427	The standard sequence assumes the merge is set up *before*
428	the close-out push.
429	
430	### vc-x1 push wrapper
431	
432	`vc-x1 push <bookmark>` wraps per-push mechanics. See
433	`vc-x1 push --help` for current flags. `<bookmark>` names a
434	work-repo bookmark only; the bot repo is always pinned to
435	`main` (see [.claude cadence](#claude-cadence)).
436	
437	**Current limitation**: only fully supports the
438	[Keep separate](#shape-at-close-out-push) shape; other
439	shapes need manual jj steps. Planned improvements are
440	project state, tracked in the project's `TODO.md` —
441	this protocol describes only the stable mechanism.
442	
443	### .claude cadence
444	
445	**Cadence**: one push = one bot-repo commit, paired
446	with every work-repo commit in that push.
447	
448	The `.claude` working copy accumulates session data
449	across the cycle; its change ID stays stable across
450	snapshots, `jj describe`, and the squash-push fold, so
451	work-repo `ochid:` trailers resolve.
452	
453	`.claude` is a linear journal — all session work lives
454	on `main`, regardless of the work-repo bookmark. **Do
455	not create or maintain bot-repo bookmarks that mirror
456	work-repo branches** — risks the bot steering session
457	pushes to the wrong remote ref.
458	
459	Ending a session: if the user runs `/exit` there will be
460	session information created, which we don't worry about.
461	The user can close the terminal instead and `@` will
462	remain empty.
463

## Pushing

### Policy

Push is **discretionary** during the cycle (backup,
progress visibility) and **mandatory at close-out** —
the cycle's result must be published.

**Approval is per-push.** Every push — any repo, any kind:
cycle push, interim backup, recovery/surgery force-push —
happens only after the user has reviewed the changes to be
published and explicitly approved that specific push.
Approval of a plan that *includes* a push does not authorize
the push itself; stop and ask again at the moment of pushing.

**Default is interactive; an explicit scoped delegation waives
the gates.** The gates above — per-push approval, the
commit-description review (show title+body and stop), and the
hard stop after push/squash-push — are the *interactive
default*.
They yield when the user **explicitly** delegates a complete,
bounded task and authorizes carrying it through ("do all of X
and push each step, don't check in"). The bot then proceeds
through that task's commits and pushes without stopping, and
continues past each push to the next step. Conditions:

- **Explicit grant** — never inferred from a task merely being
  well-scoped; the user's words must authorize unattended
  completion. "Commit and push" (or "then push") names the
  destination, not a waiver: it authorizes the push *after*
  the normal work review and description review, not skipping
  them. Only wording that explicitly waives the stops ("don't
  check in", "no need to review", "carry it through
  unattended") waives them.
- **Bounded goal** — covers the named task only; does not carry
  to the next task or a vaguer follow-on.
- **Destructive ops still pause** — delegation covers the task's
  ordinary commits and pushes; it does *not* pre-authorize a
  genuinely irreversible action (force-push over published
  history, history rewrite, deleting a remote branch). Those can
  permanently destroy work and aren't a normal cycle step, so the
  bot flags one before acting. An ordinary delegated cycle never
  reaches this.
- **Still transparent** — report each commit/push as it lands
  (title + outcome) so the user can catch up.
- **When in doubt, ask** — ambiguous authorization falls back to
  per-push approval.

### Shape at close-out push

At close-out the cycle's *work* is done; its *published
shape* is the remaining choice, made at push time. Surface
the options and get user approval before pushing — once on
the target, changing shape is a remote rewrite (force-push,
needs approval), so choose deliberately.

- **Squash to one commit** — single entry on the target.
  Right for straightforward changes where the Work-N is
  focused on one or two files.
- **Merge non-ff** *(current default)* — `main` gains a
  merge commit (`X.Y.Z`); cycle commits stay reachable via
  two parents. `jj log -r ..@ -n <N>` shows the trapezoidal
  shape. See [Merge non-ff recipe](#merge-non-ff-recipe)
  for the full setup sequence.
- **Keep separate** — one commit per cycle entry on
  `main`. Use when the decomposition itself is
  informative. Each chores section keeps its own header /
  `Commits:` ref; no consolidation churn.

Set up squash/merge before invoking `vc-x1 push`; use
`jj git push` directly for non-standard shapes.

### Merge non-ff recipe

Setting up a [Merge non-ff](#shape-at-close-out-push)
close-out is a fixed sequence. `<closeout>` is the cycle's
close-out commit, `<prev>` the previous cycle's close-out
(the current `main` tip), `<work-tip>` the cycle's last
Work commit:

1. **Rebase the close-out into a merge** — `jj rebase -r
   <closeout> --onto <prev> --onto <work-tip>`.
   - `-r <closeout>` keeps the `<closeout>` commit in place.
   - `--onto <prev>` becomes its first parent (trunk).
   - `--onto <work-tip>` becomes the second parent.

   Together these make `<closeout>` a merge of
   `<prev>` + `<work-tip>`, forming a trapezoidal commit.
2. **Use `jj new <merge>`** to add an empty `@` above the
   merge. The rebase left `@` *on* the now-content-bearing
   merge, which git/IDE diff views show as uncommitted;
   `jj new` restores the clean empty `@` on top.
3. **Push** — `jj git push --bookmark main -R .`.

**Post-hoc caveat.** If the cycle was already pushed
[Keep separate](#shape-at-close-out-push) its commits are
immutable: the rebase needs `--ignore-immutable` and the
push force-updates `main`.
The standard sequence assumes the merge is set up *before*
the close-out push.

### vc-x1 push wrapper

`vc-x1 push <bookmark>` wraps per-push mechanics. See
`vc-x1 push --help` for current flags. `<bookmark>` names a
work-repo bookmark only; the bot repo is always pinned to
`main` (see [.claude cadence](#claude-cadence)).

**Current limitation**: only fully supports the
[Keep separate](#shape-at-close-out-push) shape; other
shapes need manual jj steps. Planned improvements are
project state, tracked in the project's `TODO.md` —
this protocol describes only the stable mechanism.

### .claude cadence

**Cadence**: one push = one bot-repo commit, paired
with every work-repo commit in that push.

The `.claude` working copy accumulates session data
across the cycle; its change ID stays stable across
snapshots, `jj describe`, and the squash-push fold, so
work-repo `ochid:` trailers resolve.

`.claude` is a linear journal — all session work lives
on `main`, regardless of the work-repo bookmark. **Do
not create or maintain bot-repo bookmarks that mirror
work-repo branches** — risks the bot steering session
pushes to the wrong remote ref.

Ending a session: if the user runs `/exit` there will be
session information created, which we don't worry about.
The user can close the terminal instead and `@` will
remain empty.

### Recovery

- **If push exits before its last stage** — `push-work`
  succeeded but the bot-repo publish didn't run
  (`squash-push-bot` in `vc-x1 push --status` / `--from`
  stage names) — run the squash+push by hand:

  ```
  vc-x1 squash-push -R .claude
  ```

  It runs in-process, so a failure is a visible non-zero
  exit — no log file to chase.
- **Run squash-push again if `@` is non-empty** after a
  pass (also desirable after extra activity by the bot's
  agents).
  - Why: the bot keeps writing session data while the
    command runs — the invocation's own record plus any
    closing response land after the squash.
  - Safe to repeat: bot session data is append-only, so a
    re-run never conflicts or overwrites. (This could
    change; it is not under the user's control.)
  - No guarantees: events outside the bot's control can leave
    `@` non-empty — e.g. the bot's back end may decide to
    squash/consolidate session data, which can take minutes
    and land after the pass. The remedy is the same: just
    run squash-push again. This is why a single pass is never
    guaranteed to leave `@` empty.
- **Clear push's saved state** after any out-of-band
  recovery — `rm .vc-x1/push-state.toml` or `vc-x1 push
  <bookmark> --restart` — otherwise push resumes from a
  stale stage.
- **Late work-repo tweak after the work-repo push succeeded**
  (e.g. updating AGENTS.md or memory) requires `jj
  squash --ignore-immutable` and a re-push; that is a
  remote rewrite and needs explicit approval like any
  push.

content.text:
Diagnosis confirmed — here's exactly what happened and the proposed repair.

**What went wrong.** `vc-x1 push`'s `commit-work` stage assumes *it* commits the working copy. Since I had already committed 0.76.0-1 by hand, `@` was empty at push time — and unlike `commit-bot` (which skips when clean), `commit-work` committed the empty `@` anyway with the supplied title/body. So:

- `quompsuw` (`278f7950`) — the real -1 with all the content, but **no ochid** (push stamps only the topmost commit, which turned out to be the duplicate).
- `mkmzuqvp` (`cfae1ec4`) — an **empty** duplicate carrying the `ochid: /.claude/mwpwsryvpskx` trailer; the bookmark and origin point at it.
- The bot commit `mwpwsryvpskx`'s `ochid: /mkmzuqvpqmkm` points at the empty duplicate instead of the real -1.

**The good news:** `chore: open repo registry cycle` (`da932d22`) is *not* missing — I verified it's an ancestor of the pushed tip on `refactor-vc-x1@origin`. The two identical `0.76.0-1` titles just push it below the fold in the GitHub list.

**Proposed repair** (rewrites published history on both repos, so per policy I need your explicit approval):

1. Work repo: re-describe `quompsuw` (`--ignore-immutable`) appending the trailer `ochid: /.claude/mwpwsryvpskx`; abandon the empty `mkmzuqvp`; `jj bookmark set refactor-vc-x1 -r quompsuw --allow-backwards`; force-push the bookmark.
2. Bot repo: re-describe `mwpwsryvpskx` (`--ignore-immutable`) changing its trailer to `ochid: /quompsuwrqys` (chids survive the rewrites, so both pointers stay valid); push `main`.
3. Verify with `validate-desc` on both sides and the logs.

**Root cause follow-up:** this is a real `vc-x1 push` bug — `commit-work` should skip an empty `@` like `commit-bot` does (or error loudly rather than minting a stamped empty commit). Since 0.77.0 (`split push.rs + stateless push`) rebuilds exactly this code, I'd record it in `notes/bugs.md` now and fix it there rather than as another rider. The process lesson for the meantime, which I'll follow: when the work commit is pre-committed by hand, hand-write its ochid and expect push's message stage to apply to the bot side only.

Approve the two force-pushes and I'll run the repair.

13	   `refs/heads/master`.** The only branch pushed is `main`,
14	   so a later `jj git clone` of that bare repo has no default
15	   branch to auto-track and `vc-x1 clone` fails its

17	   remote 'main@origin'"). Found building `tests/cli_sync.rs`
18	   (worked around there with `git symbolic-ref HEAD
19	   refs/heads/main`).
20	   - **Fix direction:** init's local bare provisioning sets
21	     HEAD to `refs/heads/main` at creation.
22	
23	2. **`clone` session-remote derivation mismatches init's
24	   local naming; relative TARGET breaks the session clone.**
25	   Two related defects, both found building
26	   `tests/cli_sync.rs`:
27	   - `derive_session_url` maps `<x>.git` →
28	     `<x>.claude.git`, but `init --repo local` names the
29	     session remote `remote-claude.git` — so a dual clone of
30	     a locally-init'd project's `remote-code.git` looks for
31	     `remote-code.claude.git` and fails.
32	   - A relative local-path TARGET fails on the session side
33	     regardless: `clone_dual` runs the session `jj git
34	     clone` with the just-cloned code repo as cwd, so the
35	     relative source no longer resolves. Workaround: pass an
36	     absolute TARGET.
37	
38	3. **`push` `bookmark-set` races the git index lock.**
39	   `jj bookmark set` on the colocated work repo failed twice
40	   (the 0.69.0-3 and 0.69.0-4 pushes, same stage) with
41	   "Failed to reset Git HEAD state … could not acquire lock
42	   for `.git/index` … after 1 attempt(s)"; the lockfile was
43	   already gone on inspection seconds later.
44	   - **Cost:** push aborts mid-flow (rollback restored both
45	     repos cleanly both times); recovery is a `--restart`
46	     rerun, which succeeded both times.
47	   - The bot thinks a git-aware watcher (shell prompt,
48	     editor) briefly re-reads the repo after the commit
49	     stages touch `.git`, holding the index lock exactly
50	     when `bookmark-set` resets git HEAD; jj gives up after
51	     a single attempt.
52	   - **Fix direction** (two options, possibly combined):
53	     - retry with short backoff around the bookmark-set
54	       stage (or all jj invocations that reset git HEAD
55	       state)
56	     - use jj-lib in-process instead of spawning `jj`
57	       commands (suggested 2026-07-15) — the lock
58	       contention is external, so this alone doesn't
59	       remove the race, but the retry loop becomes ours
60	       (catch the lock error, back off, retry) with real
61	       error types instead of stderr parsing; this is the
62	       refactor program's
63	       [jj-lib migration stage](refactor-20260716.md#stage-jj-lib-migration)
64	
65	4. **stdout output panics on a closed pipe (EPIPE).**
66	   `vc-x1 bot-session <file> | head` panics once `head`
67	   closes the pipe: the logger's `println!` aborts with
68	   "failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe". Repo-wide
69	   behavior of the `info!` → `println!` path, but
70	   bot-session (0.70.0-2) is the first subcommand whose
71	   output routinely feeds a pager/filter. Found during
72	   0.70.0-2 verification.
73	   - **Cost:** ugly panic + backtrace hint instead of the
74	     Unix-conventional silent exit; output before the pipe
75	     closed is intact.
76	   - **Fix direction:** handle EPIPE in the logger (write
77	     via `writeln!` to a locked stdout and exit 0 on
78	     `BrokenPipe`), or reset SIGPIPE to default on unix at
79	     startup.
80	5. **`push` resume-after-rollback replays from the wrong
81	   stage.** Observed at the 0.75.0-2 push (2026-07-23): the
82	   bookmark-set lock race (Bugs #3) fired, the error path
83	   `op restore`d both repos — undoing `commit-work` /
84	   `commit-bot` — but the state file still said
85	   `stage = bookmark-set`. The rerun resumed there,
86	   *skipping the commit stages*: bookmark-set pinned the
87	   bookmarks to `@-` (the **previous** cycle commit),
88	   push-work no-op re-pushed it, and squash-push-bot
89	   squashed the accumulated session data into the
90	   already-published previous bot commit and republished
91	   it. The completion sanity check caught the chid
92	   mismatch and warned, but after the damage.
93	   - **Cost:** no data loss (work `@` kept the uncommitted
94	     changes; the bot chid is rebase-stable so the ochid
95	     pairing survived) — but session data landed under the
96	     previous commit's title, and the published bot commit
97	     was rewritten in place.
98	   - The state file and the op-restore rollback disagree
99	     about where the run stopped: rollback rewinds the
100	     *repos* to pre-commit, but not the *state* to the
101	     `message` stage. Any `Err` between `commit-work` and
102	     the stage save has the same shape.
103	   - **Fix direction:** on rollback, rewind (or delete) the
104	     state file in the same breath — or retire the state
105	     file entirely and derive resume from repo reality,
106	     which is the refactor program's
107	     [stateless push stage](refactor-20260716.md#stage-stateless-push);

# Bugs

Known defects we're aware of but haven't scheduled a fix for.
Each entry describes what goes wrong, when, and the cost of
the failure. Entries are numbered (`1.` `2.` …) the same way
as `## Todo` in `TODO.md`; run
`vc-x1 fix-todo --no-dry-run notes/bugs.md` to renumber after
insert / delete / reorder.

## Bugs

1. **`init --repo local` bare remotes keep HEAD at
   `refs/heads/master`.** The only branch pushed is `main`,
   so a later `jj git clone` of that bare repo has no default
   branch to auto-track and `vc-x1 clone` fails its
   `verify_tracking` check ("bookmark 'main' has non-tracking
   remote 'main@origin'"). Found building `tests/cli_sync.rs`
   (worked around there with `git symbolic-ref HEAD
   refs/heads/main`).
   - **Fix direction:** init's local bare provisioning sets
     HEAD to `refs/heads/main` at creation. Scheduled with
     the repo-registry cycle's de-gitify init rung
     (0.76.0-5), which rebuilds that provisioning
     ([the stage](refactor-20260716.md#stage-de-gitify-init)).

2. **`clone` session-remote derivation mismatches init's
   local naming; relative TARGET breaks the session clone.**
   Two related defects, both found building
   `tests/cli_sync.rs`:
   - `derive_session_url` maps `<x>.git` →
     `<x>.claude.git`, but `init --repo local` names the
     session remote `remote-claude.git` — so a dual clone of
     a locally-init'd project's `remote-code.git` looks for
     `remote-code.claude.git` and fails.
   - A relative local-path TARGET fails on the session side
     regardless: `clone_dual` runs the session `jj git
     clone` with the just-cloned code repo as cwd, so the
     relative source no longer resolves. Workaround: pass an
     absolute TARGET.

3. **`push` `bookmark-set` races the git index lock.**
   `jj bookmark set` on the colocated work repo failed twice
   (the 0.69.0-3 and 0.69.0-4 pushes, same stage) with
   "Failed to reset Git HEAD state … could not acquire lock
   for `.git/index` … after 1 attempt(s)"; the lockfile was
   already gone on inspection seconds later.
   - **Cost:** push aborts mid-flow (rollback restored both
     repos cleanly both times); recovery is a `--restart`
     rerun, which succeeded both times.
   - The bot thinks a git-aware watcher (shell prompt,
     editor) briefly re-reads the repo after the commit
     stages touch `.git`, holding the index lock exactly
     when `bookmark-set` resets git HEAD; jj gives up after
     a single attempt.
   - **Fix direction** (two options, possibly combined):
     - retry with short backoff around the bookmark-set
       stage (or all jj invocations that reset git HEAD
       state)
     - use jj-lib in-process instead of spawning `jj`
       commands (suggested 2026-07-15) — the lock
       contention is external, so this alone doesn't
       remove the race, but the retry loop becomes ours
       (catch the lock error, back off, retry) with real
       error types instead of stderr parsing; this is the
       refactor program's
       [jj-lib migration stage](refactor-20260716.md#stage-jj-lib-migration)

4. **stdout output panics on a closed pipe (EPIPE).**
   `vc-x1 bot-session <file> | head` panics once `head`
   closes the pipe: the logger's `println!` aborts with
   "failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe". Repo-wide
   behavior of the `info!` → `println!` path, but
   bot-session (0.70.0-2) is the first subcommand whose
   output routinely feeds a pager/filter. Found during
   0.70.0-2 verification.
   - **Cost:** ugly panic + backtrace hint instead of the
     Unix-conventional silent exit; output before the pipe
     closed is intact.
   - **Fix direction:** handle EPIPE in the logger (write
     via `writeln!` to a locked stdout and exit 0 on
     `BrokenPipe`), or reset SIGPIPE to default on unix at
     startup.
5. **`push` resume-after-rollback replays from the wrong
   stage.** Observed at the 0.75.0-2 push (2026-07-23): the
   bookmark-set lock race (Bugs #3) fired, the error path
   `op restore`d both repos — undoing `commit-work` /
   `commit-bot` — but the state file still said
   `stage = bookmark-set`. The rerun resumed there,
   *skipping the commit stages*: bookmark-set pinned the
   bookmarks to `@-` (the **previous** cycle commit),
   push-work no-op re-pushed it, and squash-push-bot
   squashed the accumulated session data into the
   already-published previous bot commit and republished
   it. The completion sanity check caught the chid
   mismatch and warned, but after the damage.
   - **Cost:** no data loss (work `@` kept the uncommitted
     changes; the bot chid is rebase-stable so the ochid
     pairing survived) — but session data landed under the
     previous commit's title, and the published bot commit
     was rewritten in place.
   - The state file and the op-restore rollback disagree
     about where the run stopped: rollback rewinds the
     *repos* to pre-commit, but not the *state* to the
     `message` stage. Any `Err` between `commit-work` and
     the stage save has the same shape.
   - **Fix direction:** on rollback, rewind (or delete) the
     state file in the same breath — or retire the state
     file entirely and derive resume from repo reality,
     which is the refactor program's
     [stateless push stage](refactor-20260716.md#stage-stateless-push);
     this incident is its strongest evidence yet.

6. **`push` `commit-work` commits an empty `@`, minting a
   duplicate stamped commit.** Observed at the 0.76.0-1 push
   (2026-07-27): the work commit had been made by hand before
   invoking `vc-x1 push`, so `@` was empty — `commit-bot`
   skips a clean repo, but `commit-work` committed the empty
   `@` anyway with the supplied `--title`/`--body`. The
   result: an empty duplicate of the real commit on top of
   it, the ochid trailer stamped on the duplicate (push
   stamps only the topmost commit), the bookmark pushed at
   the duplicate, and the bot commit's `ochid:` pointing at
   the duplicate instead of the real commit.
   - **Cost:** no data loss, but published history needed a
     dual-repo repair — describe + abandon + sideways
     force-push on both sides (`--ignore-immutable`).
   - **Fix direction:** `commit-work` skips an empty `@`
     like `commit-bot` does, and the ochid stamp then lands
     on the real topmost commit; alternatively error loudly
     when `@` is empty and no commit is needed. Fold into
     the refactor program's
     [split push.rs + stateless push stage](refactor-20260716.md#stage-split-pushrs),
     which rebuilds this code path.

One invocation = one work commit + one paired bot commit — the "commit/push cycle".

Answer to your question, with the fix now in place:

**Default resolution** (no flags) in a legacy workspace was already safe — every config-driven path hard-rejects with the `[repos]` fix-it before any label logic runs, as you saw with `config --validate`.

**The gap was the explicit `--other-repo` escape hatch** in `validate-desc`/`fix-desc`, which bypasses that rejection. There, side detection (`is_bot_dir`) only knew the new `repos.bot` self-resolution, so iiac-perf's `.claude` read as a *work* repo — your run would have flagged all 4 valid `/.claude/` trailers as wrong-prefix (I reproduced exactly that), and a `fix-desc` would have rewritten good trailers wrong.

**Fix:** `is_bot_dir` now falls back to the legacy location rule, extended to both generations — the parent config's `workspace.bot` *and* iiac-perf's pre-0.75 `workspace.other-repo` (which, to your "somewhat malformed" point, is actually well-formed for its generation: bare names were that schema's convention; the leading `/` only arrived with 0.75.x). Verified live on `~/data/prgs/rust/iiac-perf` in both directions: work→bot and bot→work now report all trailers `ok` (the `miss` rows are just the empty working copies). Covered by a new `is_bot_dir_legacy_fallback` test over both generations.

/// honors both rejected generations' bot declarations, and stays

#[test]
fn legacy_configured_bot_dir_reads_old_schemas() {
    let base = ws_tempdir("legacy-botdir");
    let root = base.join("ws");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&root).unwrap();
    // 0.75.x root-anchored schema.
    std::fs::write(
        root.join(VC_CONFIG_FILE),
        "[workspace]\nwork = \"/\"\nbot = \"/.claude\"\n",
    )
    .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        legacy_configured_bot_dir(&root),
        Some(root.join(".claude"))
    );
    // Pre-0.75.0 path/other-repo schema.
    std::fs::write(
        root.join(VC_CONFIG_FILE),
        "[workspace]\npath = \"/\"\nother-repo = \".bot\"\n",
    )
    .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(legacy_configured_bot_dir(&root), Some(root.join(".bot")));
    // Current [repos] schema → None (not legacy).
    std::fs::write(root.join(VC_CONFIG_FILE), WORK_DUAL).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(legacy_configured_bot_dir(&root), None);
    // No config at all → None.
    std::fs::remove_file(root.join(VC_CONFIG_FILE)).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(legacy_configured_bot_dir(&root), None);
    std::fs::remove_dir_all(&base).ok();
}
